name: Upland sticky rice
summary: Upland sticky rice steamed twice. The culture desk colours it red, purple, yellow, and green with leaves, tubers, and fruit it does not name. Vietnam News calls the same rice multi-colour and says a ball of it is eaten by hand. It is not cơm lam. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Dien Bien Phu. The culture desk, Vietnam News, and Vietnamnet all describe this rice. None of them says five colours, and none names the dye plants.
texture: The culture desk says the grains are plump, glossy, sweet, fragrant, and soft, and that a ball leaves the hand clean. Vietnamnet says it is steamed, not sticky on the hand, after two passes in a wooden steamer. Vietnam News says soft and aromatic when balled by hand.
howToEat: The culture desk: steam it twice in a wooden steamer. Leaves, tubers, and fruit give red, purple, yellow, and green. The plants are not named. Eat it with grilled fish or grilled pork, or carry a packet. The packet is called cóong xôi. It is not cơm lam.

Vietnamnet: soak the rice for many hours so it does not go hard. Steam it in the wooden steamer, turn it out into a basket, spread it with chopsticks, rest it, and steam it again until it is even. White rice is also described, beside the coloured rice.
Vietnam News does not print the two steamings or the colour list. It says visitors buy the rice to carry, and that the Thái table eats it with fish and pork grill.
A price is Check on arrival. A breakfast stall that sells only this rice is Check on arrival.
where: The Thái table. The carried packet is for the road. No shop is a pick. A stall hour is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Upland sticky rice in Dien Bien Phu — steamed twice
seoDescription: Xôi nếp nương, steamed twice, coloured red, purple, yellow, and green. Not five colours, and not cơm lam. A price is Check on arrival.
